Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
------------------------------------------
The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad, though not included within the group of the ten Cardinal उपनिषद्स्, is deemed so important that it is always placed in the eleventh position. It must be considered as ancient as the Muṇḍaka and the Kaṭha उपनिषद्स्.
It belongs to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It has 113 mantras included in six chapters.
Śvetāśvatara is the sage who propagated or transmitted this Upaniṣad. Three of its mantras (6.9; 4.5 and 5.8) have been discussed in the Brahmasūtras (

).
It has some special features. It has addressed परमात्मन् (Supreme Self) as Hara (1.10), रुद्र (3.2; 3.4; 4.12; 4.21 and 22) and शिव (3.14; 4.10). However scholars consider them as general names of God and hence do not concede that it is a Śaiva Upaniṣad.
The second speciality is its advocacy of भक्ति or devotion to God as an important aspect of sādhana.
The third is giving a definite form to God and consider him as a Person.
Use of the words Sāṅkhya, योग and कपिल is the next. However, these do not propagate the Sāṅkhya philosophy as described in later philosophical literature.
The general ideas found in the other उपनिषद्स् are reflected here also.
This Upaniṣad has five commentaries—written by शङ्कर (A.

-820), Vijñānātman (13th century), Śaṅkarā-नन्द (14th century), Nārāyaṇatīrtha (18th century) and Upaniṣad Brahmayogin (18th century).
See also UPANIṢADS.

Śvetaketu
------------------------------------------
Śvetaketu is one of the great sages we come across in the उपनिषद्स् and the Mahābhārata.
He was the son of गौतम आरुणि (also known as उद्दालक). In his younger days he was proud and arrogant, but had to taste defeat in the court of the king प्रवाहण जैवलि (Chāndogya Upaniṣad

-5). Later on, his ड़थेर् taught him the science of ब्रह्मन् (ibid 6).
In course of time he himself became a great teacher. उपकोसल was a talented disciple of his (vide Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.10).
Naciketa was his brother and Sujātā the wife of the sage Kahoḷa was his sister. He had married Suvarcalā, the daughter of the sage देवल.
Śvetaketu is considered to have assigned proper duties to the priests performing sacrifices.
Annoyed at the loose sexual behaviour of the people of his times, he is said to have systematised the institution of मर्रिअगे.
He also produced an abridged edition of the Kāmaśāstra (Science of Erotics) originally written by नन्दि, शिव’s famous mount.
Another famous sage, अष्टावक्र, was his nephew.
